title: The Phantom Payroll
narrative: Employees are reporting ghost salaries — payments going to names that do not exist in the HR system. The Corruptor has injected phantom records. Cross-reference the payroll database and expose every phantom entry.

levels.title: Part 1 — Survey the Payroll
levels.narrative: First, get a full picture of the payroll table. Retrieve all payroll records sorted by salary descending.
levels.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE payroll (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, employee_name TEXT NOT NULL, department TEXT, salary REAL NOT NULL, payment_date TEXT);

hints.content: Use ORDER BY to sort records. DESC means highest first.

hints.code_snippet: SELECT * FROM payroll ORDER BY salary DESC;
SELECT * FROM payroll ORDER BY salary DESC;

levels.title: Part 2 — Find the Phantoms
levels.narrative: Real employees have names like Firstname Lastname. Phantom entries contain underscores. Filter for names containing an underscore to expose the injected records.
levels.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE payroll (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, employee_name TEXT NOT NULL, department TEXT, salary REAL NOT NULL, payment_date TEXT);

hints.content: The LIKE operator with % wildcards can find patterns in text. Note: underscore is itself a LIKE wildcard, so use ESCAPE to match it literally.
Use LIKE with ESCAPE to match a literal underscore:
hints.code_snippet: SELECT * FROM payroll WHERE employee_name LIKE '%\_%' ESCAPE '\';
SELECT * FROM payroll WHERE employee_name LIKE '%\_%' ESCAPE '\';

levels.title: Part 3 — Total Phantom Drain
levels.narrative: The CFO needs the total financial damage. Sum the salaries of all phantom employees and label the result phantom_drain.
levels.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE payroll (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, employee_name TEXT NOT NULL, department TEXT, salary REAL NOT NULL, payment_date TEXT);

hints.content: SUM() is the aggregate function for totals. Combine it with the same LIKE filter from Part 2 and alias the result.
SELECT SUM(salary) AS phantom_drain FROM payroll WHERE ...
hints.code_snippet: SELECT SUM(salary) AS phantom_drain FROM payroll WHERE employee_name LIKE '%\_%' ESCAPE '\';
SELECT SUM(salary) AS phantom_drain FROM payroll WHERE employee_name LIKE '%\_%' ESCAPE '\';

levels.title: Part 4 — Department Breakdown
levels.narrative: Final report: calculate total payroll per department for all legitimate employees only (no underscores in name), sorted by total descending. This closes the case.
levels.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE payroll (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, employee_name TEXT NOT NULL, department TEXT, salary REAL NOT NULL, payment_date TEXT);

hints.content: Combine a NOT LIKE phantom filter with GROUP BY department and SUM(salary). Alias the sum as total_salary and order DESC.
SELECT department, SUM(salary) AS total_salary FROM payroll WHERE ... GROUP BY department ORDER BY total_salary DESC;
hints.code_snippet:
SELECT department, SUM(salary) AS total_salary
FROM payroll
WHERE employee_name NOT LIKE '%\_%' ESCAPE '\'
GROUP BY department
ORDER BY total_salary DESC;

SELECT department, SUM(salary) AS total_salary
FROM payroll
WHERE employee_name NOT LIKE '%\_%' ESCAPE '\'
GROUP BY department
ORDER BY total_salary DESC;
